diagnostic_evidence.quote: if $f$ has two entries $i, j$ equal to $1$ (all others $0$) ... with $\min\{m_i,m_j\}=2$
For all other tuples $f$, we have $\deg X>r$ and there exist linear space of projective dimension $r-1$ that intersects $X$ in more than $r$ real points

issues.failure_explanation: The special +1 case is not exhaustive. For ell=1, d=4, f=(2), m=2, one has n_col=3, n_codim=1, so the formula gives r(f)=1. But X is the Veronese conic in P^2, degree 2, and a generic line A spanned by two rank-one tensors intersects X in exactly two points; hence r(f)=2. The proof's claim that all other tuples have deg X>r fails here because deg X=2 and r=n_codim+1=2.

failure_location.quote:
r(f) =
\begin{cases}
\min\{\,n_{\rm col}^f,\, n_{\rm codim}^f + 1\,\}, & 
\text{if $f$ has two entries $i, j$ equal to $1$ (all others $0$)} \\[-0.5ex]
& \quad \text{with $\min\{m_i,m_j\}=2$,}\\
\min\{\,n_{\rm col}^f,\, n_{\rm codim}^f\,\}, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing exceptional cases where n_codim+1 equals the degree of X (e.g. Veronese v_2(P^1) and v_2(P^2)) or replace the formula by the correct intersection-theoretic value.
issues.overall_effect: The rank bound r(f) is too small in missing exceptional cases, so uniqueness and recovery rank guarantees based on r(f) are unreliable.
issues.title: Incomplete rank formula in Theorem rmax_formula
issues.why_classification: The formula is a central rank bound; correcting it requires additional algebraic-geometry case analysis and changes the advertised recovery ranks.

issues.failure_explanation: The function h(ν) is decreasing. For the shift γ_i = sqrt((f_i-1)/f_i) h(ν) to dominate the negative Hessian bound, one needs ν to be a lower bound on F (so h(ν) ≥ h(F)), not an upper bound. Taking ν=1 satisfies F≤ν and gives γ_i=0 for f_i>1, which is insufficient for convexity at points with F<1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace F≤ν by F≥ν (or equivalently choose ν as a lower bound on the objective along the iterates).
issues.overall_effect: The stated shift choice may not ensure the convexity needed for the global convergence guarantee of Algorithm psspm on the symmetrized tensor.
issues.title: Incorrect inequality direction in shift condition
issues.why_classification: The mathematical content survives after a local correction of the inequality direction in the condition on ν.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses |x|^{ell f_j} ≤ |x|^2, which fails when ell f_j < 2. For ell=1, f=1, take r=2, A=span{v1,v2} with orthonormal v1,v2 and w=(v1+v2)/√2. Then F_A(w)=1, max_i |<v_i,w>|=1/√2, and C=1, so the claimed upper bound F_A ≤ max_i |<v_i,w>| is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis ell f_j ≥ 2 for all j, or change the upper-bound constant to account for the sum over i.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed proximity of critical points to optimal rank-one components fails in the basic ell=1, f=1 case.
issues.title: False upper bound in Theorem added-2 for ell=1, f=1
issues.why_classification: The result is false as stated, but a comparable bound survives with an extra condition or a larger constant.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\min\{\,n_{\rm col}^f,\, n_{\rm codim}^f + 1\,\}, & 
\text{if $f$ has two entries $i, j$ equal to $1$ (all others $0$)}

issues.failure_explanation: The equality drops the exceptional +1 cases. For d=(2,2,1), f=(1,1,0), m=(2,2,2), f is symmetry-breaking. Here r(f)=2 because f has two entries 1 and min{m_1,m_2}=2, while r(d-f)=4, so min{r(f),r(d-f)}=2. But min{n_codim^f, n_codim^{d-f}}=min(1,4)=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the expression min{r(f), r(d-f)} and do not simplify it without including the exceptional +1 cases.
issues.overall_effect: The recovery rank for symmetry-breaking flattenings is understated in exceptional cases.
issues.title: Incorrect simplification in symmetry-breaking recovery rank
issues.why_classification: The false equality affects a rank-bound corollary, but the correct expression is already present and only the simplification needs repair.

issues.failure_explanation: For n=2, the threshold is 4. At k=4 the corollary chooses f=(2,1), but r(1,1)=min{4,k}=4 while r(2,1)=C(3,2)=3, so (1,1) is strictly better. The condition should be k≥4 for n=2, not k>4.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adjust the boundary condition for n=2 (e.g. use k≥4 for (1,1)) or handle the special +1 case in the comparison.
issues.overall_effect: The optimal flattening recommendation is wrong at the boundary case n=2, k=4.
issues.title: Boundary error in optimal flattening corollary
issues.why_classification: Only a boundary case in a corollary is affected; a local threshold correction restores the statement.
